html:
The Purépecha are an Indigenous people of Michoacán in western Mexico, centred on Lake Pátzcuaro. The Spanish called them Tarascans. In the 1400s they built the Tarascan state, the second largest power in Mesoamerica after the Aztecs.

From their capital, Tzintzuntzan, on the shore of the lake, their kings, the cazonci, ruled a centralised realm. Their language is unrelated to any other in Mexico. They were skilled metalworkers in copper and bronze and made fine featherwork.

The Purépecha were the one power the Aztecs never conquered; in about 1479 they crushed a huge Aztec army. After the fall of Tenochtitlan in 1521 the last king, Tangaxuan II, submitted to Spain peacefully, but in 1530 the conquistador Nuño de Guzmán had him tortured and burned. The bishop Vasco de Quiroga then organised Purépecha towns around crafts, and many villages still keep the crafts he assigned them.
